Purpose:
Provide a framework for monitoring ICU capacity and identifying
potential capacity pressure.

Operational guidance:
ICU occupancy below 70 percent represents routine operational
conditions for this prototype.

ICU occupancy between 70 and 80 percent requires increased
monitoring of bed utilization.

ICU occupancy between 80 and 90 percent indicates elevated
capacity pressure and preparation for additional capacity.

Purpose:
Provide operational guidance for identifying ICU staffing pressure.

Operational guidance:
A shortage flag indicates that available staffing is below the
prototype operational requirement.

When a staffing shortage is detected, administrators should review
current staffing levels, upcoming shifts and possible workforce
redistribution.

If staffing pressure occurs together with high ICU occupancy,
capacity escalation should receive additional attention.

Purpose:
Provide operational guidance for monitoring emergency department
inflow.

High emergency department arrivals may create downstream pressure
on inpatient and critical-care capacity.

When emergency arrivals increase substantially, administrators
should monitor admission rates, available beds and expected
patient transfers.

Recommended actions:
Monitor emergency inflow.
Review available inpatient capacity.
Evaluate expected admissions.
Coordinate with bed-management personnel.

Purpose:
Provide operational guidance for monitoring ventilator resource
availability.

Low ventilator availability indicates increasing equipment
pressure.

When available ventilators fall below the prototype threshold,
administrators should review current utilization and expected
near-term demand.

Recommended actions:
Monitor ventilator utilization.
Review equipment availability.
Evaluate expected demand.
Escalate resource monitoring when availability becomes critically

Purpose:
Support hospital-wide monitoring of bed utilization.

Bed-management teams should continuously monitor occupied beds,
available beds, admissions, discharges and transfers.

When occupancy increases rapidly, expected discharges and
transfers should be reviewed.

Recommended actions:
Monitor available beds.
Review expected discharges.
Coordinate interdepartmental transfers.
Monitor emergency admission pressure.

Purpose:
Provide an operational framework for considering elective surgery
activity during periods of hospital capacity pressure.

When critical-care capacity becomes constrained, administrators
should review upcoming elective procedures and expected resource
requirements.

Recommended actions:
Review scheduled elective procedures.
Evaluate expected ICU resource requirements.
Coordinate surgery scheduling with available capacity.
